title: Vertical Can Pump

introduction.definition: A vertical can pump is a vertical turbine pump installed inside a closed suction vessel (the "can"), so the bowl assembly is fed from pressurised or low-NPSH piping instead of an open sump. The extra length of the can adds static head above the first impeller, giving very low NPSH required at the suction flange. It is API 610 type VS6 (diffuser) or VS7 (volute).
applications: Process pumps with very low NPSHa
key_points: Suction and discharge both at the head, above ground
introduction.summary: A multistage vertical turbine (diffuser) pump installed inside a pressurised suction can (barrel). Suction and discharge both connect to the head at grade; the liquid fills the can, flows down outside the column and bowls and enters the first-stage impeller at the bottom. Because the first stage sits well below grade, the static liquid height in the can adds to NPSH available — the main reason to choose a can pump for liquids near their boiling point.

what_to_look_for: Liquid enters the suction nozzle on the discharge head and flows down the annulus between the can and the column.
At the bottom it turns up into the suction bell; the height of liquid above the first impeller adds to NPSHa.
The bowl stages raise the pressure stage by stage.

steps.text: Liquid enters the suction nozzle on the discharge head and flows down the annulus between the can and the column.
At the bottom it turns up into the suction bell; the height of liquid above the first impeller adds to NPSHa.
The bowl stages raise the pressure stage by stage.
The column carries the pressurised liquid up to the discharge nozzle.
The mechanical seal in the head seals the shaft; the motor thrust bearing carries the down-thrust.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: As vertical turbine pumps — stage heads add; NPSHr at the flange is low because of the can depth.

script.narration: This module introduces the Vertical Can Pump.
A vertical can pump is a vertical turbine pump installed inside a closed suction vessel (the "can"), so the bowl assembly is fed from pressurised or low-NPSH piping instead of an open sump.
The extra length of the can adds static head above the first impeller, giving very low NPSH required at the suction flange.
It is API 610 type VS6 (diffuser) or VS7 (volute).
Typical applications include condensate extraction in power plants; LPG, ammonia and light-hydrocarbon loading; pipeline booster service; process pumps with very low NPSHa.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Discharge Case (Top Bowl), Bowl – Stage 1, Bowl Wear Ring – Stage 1, Impeller – Stage 1.

video_tutorials.title: Vertical Can Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Vertical Can Pump.
Check seal leakage and head vibration.
Check thrust-bearing temperature.
Verify that the can vent is open and clear.
Lift the pump out of the can; inspect bowls, impellers and bearings.
Watch for vapour lock / loss of prime: pump fails to deliver after start. Common cause: blocked can vent.
Watch for first-stage cavitation: noise, falling head. Common cause: low suction vessel level.
Watch for bearing wear: vibration. Common cause: dry running or solids.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.

questions.question: What provides the extra NPSH in a can pump?
options: The depth of the can — liquid height above the first impeller
questions.explanation: The first stage sits low in the can, so static head adds to NPSHa.

questions.question: Which API 610 type is a vertical can pump with diffuser bowls?
questions.explanation: VS6 = double-casing diffuser; VS7 = double-casing volute.

questions.question: Why must the can be vented?
options: Trapped vapour/gas can block flow to the first stage

questions.question: Where are the suction and discharge nozzles?
options: At the bottom of the can
Both on the discharge head above ground
Suction at the bell, discharge at the motor

questions.question: A typical power-plant application of can pumps is…
